BOW.Quote: Nests often attract the attention of extra adults that associate with a pair for up to an entire breeding season; these extra birds are sometimes tolerated and occasionally lead to polygyny (217). In New York, extra birds were predominantly males (219, 325), whereas in Washington, extra birds were yearling females (217). Extra adults contribute relatively little to feeding young, but they are known to mob predators and assist in nest-building, incubation, and brooding young (219, 325, 217). Extra adults may be using nest attendance as a breeding strategy either to replace one pair member should something happen to it (217) or to commit sexually selected infanticide (219, 325), providing an opportunity for males to take over the breeding female (see Behavior: Sexual Behavior). Nests that are attended by helpers often are ones occupied by older females (325), consistent with the interpretation that male attendants are trying to secure high-quality females as mates.
